mechanism: Authors declare a tree of elements and attributes. The browser's HTML parser (tokenizer → tree builder → DOM) is the execution. There is no user-level evaluation order beyond parse/reparse and script-blocking rules.
why: The web needed a durable, round-trippable document format that non-programmers could write and that browsers could recover from when markup was sloppy.
useWhen: Document structure, forms, accessibility trees, and anything that must round-trip as a web page.
price: No computation. Behaviour lives in JS, CSS, and the engine. Invalid markup is repaired, which hides errors.
